title: ParkFlow demo video v2

chapters.name: When the car park is full

vo: Your parking data may be telling you more than you think.
Saturday, 2 pm. Aina's film starts at 2:30, and level one is full.
The member bays sit empty, and nothing tells her where the free spaces are.
Twelve minutes later, she's still circling.
The car park wasn't out of bays. It was out of information.
This is ParkFlow, from Team Hexa, Universiti Malaya.
Why start on the phone? Every choice made before the ramp is one less car circling inside.
Park shows free bays on every level and how busy the next hour looks. Reserve books Ladies' parking or member bays only.
My car finds your car and pays. Your account holds membership, points and your cars.
And every trip starts with one button: I'm on my way.
Why treat members differently? Malls reward members everywhere except the first thing they do: parking.
And VIP bays sit empty while others circle.
So we give members certainty, not extra space. Same trip, two drivers.
The Gold member books a designated member bay, checked against their account and held for 15 minutes plus 10 minutes' grace.
The non-member gets the same live counts and the same guidance. Only the member bays stay locked.
At the exit, the member's first hour is free. A benefit they feel on every visit, and a reason to join.
Why ask when you'll arrive? A zone with three free bays now can be full in ten minutes, if everyone is sent there.
So ParkFlow plans for the moment you arrive, and checks again at the barrier.
In the last 15 minutes, the forecast changed two of eleven picks, steering cars away from a zone about to fill.
Why prevent instead of react? Once a queue reaches the ramp, every circling car blocks the next one.
So the trips from the app become data, joined with typical Saturdays, cinema sessions, events and promotions.
At 2:08, history alone expects 22 cars in the next half hour. ParkFlow expects 69, an hour before the peak.
The operator can pause the free-parking promotion, or ask drivers on the way to come 30 minutes later. Nothing happens until they confirm.
Act at 2:10 and the car park never passes 95%. Wait until 2:42 and it still does. Early data is the cheapest fix.
Underground, the plate camera reads the car and the barrier opens. No ticket.
The operator sees the route in the live 3D twin, and the driver sees the same instruction on their phone.
Why explain every pick? Because no operator trusts a black box. ParkFlow scores each zone on free bays, the walk, the drive and traffic, in plain words.
Gate to bay in under a minute. And the trip becomes data for the next forecast.
Why no new hardware? Because sensors and locks in every bay make parking upgrades slow and expensive.
A modern mall already has CCTV, number-plate cameras, a boom gate, level signs and a rewards app.
ParkFlow is the software that connects them, so a pilot can start in one zone without touching a bay.
With a booking, the bay is already waiting under a purple light.
The plate checks the booking in at the gate, and the car drives straight to its bay. No search at all.
Why hold it for only 25 minutes? Because a reservation that never expires is just a VIP bay again. No-shows go straight back to the pool.
Why not just switch on the FULL sign? Because that only moves the queue onto the street.
ParkFlow warns drivers before they set off, while there's still time to change plans.
Inside, it reads its own data. A driver who just paid will leave within minutes, so the next car is sent where a space is about to open.
Drivers still on the way can take an overflow car park and shuttle. At 99% full, nobody in our simulation gave up.
ParkFlow, by Team Hexa, Universiti Malaya.
Your parking data may be telling you more than you think.
